# Fixtures

Small C programs, built by clang and lld for x86-64 and x86 without a C runtime, and the binaries
they produce. The tests of every crate read them, so the binaries are committed and the tests need
no compiler. `build.ps1` rebuilds them; `/Brepro` keeps a rebuild byte-identical for the same LLVM.

| Source | Binaries | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `src/hello.c` | `hello64.exe`, `hello32.exe` | Three imports, two leaf functions, one caller |
| `src/control.c` | `control64.exe`, `control32.exe` | Loops, if-else, a dense switch, recursion, a table of function pointers, globals, a no-return call mid-function; a CodeView record |
| the three binaries above | `hello32-upx.exe`, `hello64-upx.exe`, `control32-upx.exe` | The same programs packed by `upx --best` (5.3.0): sections `UPX0`, `UPX1`, `UPX2`, the code is the unpacking stub; they print what their twins print, so `expected/hello.txt` and `expected/control.txt` are theirs too |
| `src/float.c` | `float64.exe`, `float32.exe` | Floating-point arithmetic, conversions and compares |
| `src/classes.cpp` | `classes64.exe`, `classes32.exe` | C++ with RTTI: a base, a derived class, a second base and a class with two vtables, called through base pointers; no C++ runtime |
| `src/throws.cpp` | `throws64.exe` | C++ exceptions: a throw caught by value and one by reference to a base through a function without a handler, a rethrow into a catch-all, and a local destroyed on the way out; vcruntime's throw and frame handler, nothing else of a runtime |
| `src/exports.c`, `src/exports.def` | `exports64.dll`, `exports32.dll` | Named exports, an export by ordinal only, a forwarder |
| `src/exports_host.c` | `exports_host64.exe`, `exports_host32.exe` | The program that loads the DLL its command line names and calls its exports by name and ordinal, reads the data export and checks the forwarder; the pipeline runs it over the port of `exports` and over `exports` itself |
| `src/tls.c` | `tls64.exe`, `tls32.exe` | A `__declspec(thread)` counter stepped from two threads, with the TLS directory (index, template bounds, a callback) the program defines itself for want of a C runtime |
| `src/structs.c` | `structs64.exe`, `structs32.exe` | A record of mixed fields filled and read through a pointer, for the type recovery |
| `src/dispatch.c` | `dispatch64.exe`, `dispatch32.exe` | Function-pointer dispatch through a table filled at run time under computed keys (a tail jump through a register on x64, a call through the table on x86), which no reading of the image resolves: the fixture of the trace-driven facts, whose port reads as direct calls after a traced run |
| `src/computed.c` | `computed64.exe`, `computed32.exe` | Three functions reached only through addresses computed at run time, the image's base plus an offset read from a table of masked offsets; nothing in the image refers to them (no call, no pointer, no relocation, no unwind entry), so the analysis does not find them and the call is a trap until a run supplies its target |
| `src/window.c` | `window64.exe`, `window32.exe` | A window: a class whose procedure user32 calls back, a popup of a known client size, one paint through `BeginPaint`, and a message loop ended by `PostQuitMessage`; the log names the messages whose order is the window's own and the quit code |
| `src/xbe.c` | `xbe32.xbe` | A homebrew program of the original Xbox: the kernel reached through the thunk table of the XBE header (`DbgPrint`, the pool, the return to the dashboard), no XAPI, no C runtime; the PE clang links at the Xbox's base, rewritten as an XBE by the writer in `crates/ra-asm-pe/tests/xbe.rs`, with the PE's map beside it; its expected output is the same source built for this machine with `-DXBE_HOST` |
| `src/hello.c`, `src/control.c` over `src/freestanding` | `hello_mipsel`, `control_mipsel` | The same two programs as static MIPS32 little-endian Linux executables, built by `src/freestanding/build.sh` in WSL with no C library: `freestanding/` holds a start routine per machine, `write` and `exit` by syscall, a printf of `%d %u %x %s %c`, and a `windows.h` that puts the two sources' five API calls over those. They run in `qemu-mipsel-static`, which is where their output was checked against `expected/hello.txt` and `expected/control.txt` (across line endings); `MANIFEST.toml` records the hashes, the command and the tools |
| `mips/control.c` | `mips/control` | `src/control.c` as one static MIPS32 little-endian Linux executable (o32, ISA II, no PIC, no abicalls), with its own `_start` and `write`/`exit` over `syscall`, built in WSL by the command at the top of the source; `--emit-relocs` keeps its `R_MIPS_32`, `R_MIPS_26` and `HI16`/`LO16` relocations, and its small globals sit at `$gp`. The fixture of the MIPS loader: `crates/ra-asm-pe/tests` compare its sections, entry point and `gp` with `llvm-readobj`. `mips/control.txt` is what the source prints, with LF line ends; no emulator ran it |
| `mips/control.c` | `mips/control.be` | The same program big-endian: the source's command with `--target=mips-linux-gnu` and `-mno-gpopt` (WSL's clang 18 fails to select a `$gp`-relative address on big-endian MIPS), so its globals are reached by `lui`/`addiu` pairs rather than at `$gp`. The fixture of the big-endian image: `crates/ra-asm-pe` reads its values big-endian and `crates/ra-asm-lift/tests/interp.rs` runs it at every level printing `mips/control.txt` |
| `psp/hello.c`, `psp/Makefile` | `psp/hello.prx` | A user-mode PSP module (`ET_PRX`, Allegrex little-endian) built by the PSPSDK `Makefile` with `BUILD_PRX = 1` in WSL with pspdev (the command at the top of the `Makefile`): it prints a line and a sum with `sceIoWrite(1, ...)` and leaves by `sceKernelExitGame`. Linked at zero, it loads at `0x08804000` with its `R_MIPS_32`, `R_MIPS_26` and `HI16`/`LO16` records applied; its 43 imports from nine libraries are NIDs, which `psp/nids.sh` (run once in WSL) names from the SDK's stub archives into `crates/ra-asm-pe/src/psp_nids.rs`. `psp/hello.txt` is what the source prints; no emulator ran it |
| `psp/draw.c`, `psp/Makefile` | `psp/draw.prx` | The PSP runtime's fixture, the same build with `TARGET=draw`: it names a 32-bit frame buffer in the video memory to the display, draws a line, three blocks and a square into it through the uncached mirror, reads the controller and waits for the vertical blank each frame; the square moves while a direction is held and the cross button prints its place. `crates/ra-asm-lift/tests/interp.rs` runs it headless under a pad script: `psp/draw.txt` is what it prints then, and its eighth frame is checked at the pixels the source draws. No emulator ran it |
| `psx/hello.c`, `psx/CMakeLists.txt` | `psx/hello.exe` | The PlayStation loader's fixture: a PS-X EXE (R3000 little-endian) built by the PSn00bSDK 0.24 template's `psn00bsdk_add_executable(hello GPREL hello.c)` in WSL (`cmake -S testdata/psx -B out/psx -G Ninja -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=<sdk>/lib/libpsn00b/cmake/sdk.cmake`, then `cmake --build out/psx`, with the SDK's `bin` on the path): its text of `0x800` bytes at `0x80010000`, `pc` at `_start` (`0x80010094`), no `gp` or stack in the header. It prints two lines through the SDK's `printf`, which ends in the BIOS's `putchar`; `psx/hello.txt` is what the source prints, no emulator ran it. `crates/ra-asm-pe/tests` check the header, the mirrors of RAM and the refusals of a cut header |
| `ps2/hello.c`, `ps2/Makefile` | `ps2/hello.elf` | The PlayStation 2 loader's fixture: an EE program (R5900 little-endian, n32, MIPS III, `EF_MIPS_MACH_5900`) built by a `Makefile` over ps2sdk's `samples/Makefile.pref` and `Makefile.eeglobal` in WSL with ps2dev (the command at the top of the `Makefile`; the debug sections of the SDK's libraries are stripped, the symbols kept), linked at `0x00100000` by the SDK's linkfile with `_start` at `0x00100b48` and `gp` at `0x1290f0`. It prints two lines through `sio_puts`, the EE's serial port (the transmit FIFO at `0x1000f180`), since `printf` goes through the IOP's fileio RPC and nothing of the IOP runs in the interpreter; `sio_puts` ends each line in CR LF, and `ps2/hello.txt`, written from the source with LF line ends, is compared across them. No emulator ran it. `crates/ra-asm-pe/tests` compare its sections, entry point and `gp` with `llvm-readobj` and check the folds of the memory map |
| `dc/hello.c`, `dc/Makefile` | `dc/1ST_READ.BIN`, `dc/1ST_READ.scrambled` | The Dreamcast loader's fixture: a KallistiOS program (SH-4 little-endian) built by the `Makefile` over KOS's `Makefile.rules` in WSL (the command at the top of the `Makefile`), its ELF `hello.elf` copied to the plain boot program `1ST_READ.BIN` and scrambled by KOS's `scramble` into the form a disc of the CD-ROM kind carries. The boot ROM loads it at `0x8c010000` and enters its first byte; it has no header, so `ras` takes a file named `1ST_READ.BIN` as one. It prints two lines through `printf`, which KOS's dbgio sends to the serial port; `dc/hello.txt` is what the source prints, no emulator ran it. `crates/ra-asm-pe/tests` check the mapping, the unscrambled form against the plain one and the folds of the memory map |
| `n64/hello.c`, `n64/Makefile` | `n64/hello.z64`, `n64/hello.elf` | The Nintendo 64 loader's fixture: a libdragon program (VR4300 big-endian) built by the `Makefile` over `$(N64_INST)/include/n64.mk` in WSL (the command at the top of the `Makefile`), the ROM titled `rhipper hello` with libdragon's own boot code, of no Nintendo CIC, which loads the uncompressed ELF it finds at ROM offset `0x1d00` by its segments; `hello.elf` is the same program with its debug sections stripped, whose symbols place `_start` at `0x80000400` and `main` at `0x8000ea00`. It prints two lines with `debugf`, which `debug_init_emulog` sends to the ISViewer buffer at `0xb3ff0020`; `n64/hello.txt` is what the source prints, no emulator ran it. `crates/ra-asm-pe/tests` check the ROM's program against the ELF's sections, the `.v64` and `.n64` byte orders made from it and the folds of the memory map; `apps/ras/tests/n64.rs` the platform `ras info` prints |
| `n64/draw.c`, `n64/Makefile` | `n64/draw.z64`, `n64/draw.elf` | The Nintendo 64 runtime's fixture, built as the hello is (`N64_INST=/opt/libdragon make -C testdata/n64`): libdragon's display, graphics and joypad modules. It draws a band, a line and a square into the 16-bit frame buffers `display_get` hands out, which waits for the video interface's interrupt, and reads the first controller through the joypad module, which speaks to the PIF by the serial interface's interrupt; the square moves while a direction is held and the A button prints its place. `crates/ra-asm-lift/tests/interp.rs` runs it headless under a pad script: `n64/draw.txt` is what it prints then, and its eighth frame is checked at the pixels the source draws. No emulator ran it |
| `src/psx/hello.c`, `src/psx/gte.c` | `hello_psx.exe`, `gte_psx.exe` | Two PlayStation programs (PS-EXE, MIPS R3000 little-endian) built by `src/psx/build.sh` in WSL with PSn00bSDK 0.24: `hello` prints one line through the BIOS's printf; `gte` sends a cube's eight vertices through the GTE (`RTPT`, `RTPS`, `NCLIP`, `AVSZ3`, the control registers by `ctc2`) and prints the screen coordinates, depths and the flag register, with two vertices that overflow the division and saturate the coordinates. No emulator is on the machine: `expected/hello_psx.txt` is what the source formats and `expected/gte_psx.txt` the GTE's documented arithmetic over inputs chosen to be exact (evidence `source` in `MANIFEST.toml`, which says what replaces it). The symbol map beside each is `nm` over the ELF |
| `rhtest/src/core.c` | `rhtest/core-O2.exe`, `rhtest/core-Od.exe` | The old pipeline's test program: integers, branches, loops, recursion, switches, arrays, structs by value and through a hidden pointer, globals, strings, a linked list, packed and punned layouts |
| `rhtest/src/<name>.c`, `.cpp` | `rhtest/<name>-clang.exe` | The other fifteen rhtest programs, built here by `rhtest/build.ps1` with clang-cl over the MSVC C runtime (`/O2 /MD`): `calls`, `int64`, `float`, `fpenv`, `crt` port and run; `misc`, `sys`, `win`, `seh`, `eh`, `cpp`, `com`, `stl`, `stlio`, `engine` wait for what the last paragraph below names |
| `rhtest/src/core.c`, `int64.c` | `rhtest/core-static.exe`, `rhtest/int64-static.exe` | The same by clang-cl at `/O2 /MT`: the C runtime linked into the image, no PDB, only the map, as a VS2010 `/MT` program ships. The runtime's functions are recognized by the map's libraries and left to the host, the startup is the driver's, and the x86 helpers (`_alldiv`, the stack probe, the cookie check) stay the program's |

Beside each binary is the linker map (`.map`): the analysis tests compare the functions they find
with it. `expected/<name>.txt` is what the program prints when it runs natively; the execution
oracle compares the lifted program with it. `MANIFEST.toml` is the record of how every committed
binary, vector file and expected output was made and what it rests on (`native`, `emulator` or
`source`); `cargo test -p ra-asm-testing --test manifest` hashes the tree and fails on a wrong
hash and on a file under `bin`, `expected`, `rhtest` or `vectors` (`.vec`, `.cases`) that is not
listed, printing the hash its entry takes: a new fixture comes with its entry.

`xbe32.xbe` runs through the IR interpreter only, which answers its kernel calls itself; its port
over clang waits for a platform runtime that defines the kernel's exports for the host. The XDK's
libraries (`xapilib.lib`, `d3d8.lib`) are not here: a program that links them is recognized the
way the C runtime's static libraries are, by signatures taken from the `.lib` files
(`SignatureSet::from_library`), when the SDK is on the machine.

`rhtest/` holds the old pipeline's test programs: `rhtest/src` is their source (each program
defines `rhtest_run()` over `rhtest.h`; `rhtest_main.c`, linked into each, prints every check and
a checksum through `WriteFile`), built with MSVC 14.51 for x86 at `/O2` and `/Od` against the C
runtime DLLs, as `<name>-O2.exe` and `<name>-Od.exe` with a link map each, and by clang-cl
(`rhtest/build.ps1`, `/O2 /MD` over the same runtime: the program's code is clang's, the startup
and the helpers are MSVC's) as `<name>-clang.exe`. `<name>.txt` is the native output, with the
exit code (the checksum's low seven bits) as its last line (`cargo test -p ra-asm-emit --test
oracle rhtest_write_references -- --ignored` writes a missing one); the emit oracle ports each
variant as C and as Rust and compares both the output and the exit code. The machine and promoted
levels do not run them: a 32-bit program that starts through the C runtime needs the standalone
port. The Visual Studio 2010 builds (`cl` 16.00 at `/MT`, the toolset of a VS2010 game client) go
beside the others as `<name>-vs2010.exe` with their maps, built elsewhere like the `-O2` and `-Od`
ones; the emit oracle's `rhtest_<name>_vs2010_*` tests run `core` and `int64` when the binary is
there and skip with a message when it is not.

What the programs still waiting for need, each an `ignored` test naming it: `seh` and `eh` the
exception handling of milestone J (task 49); `misc`, `sys` and `win` the Win32 structures laid out
apart on x86 and x64 (`WNDCLASS`, `MSG`, `OVERLAPPED`, `SLIST`, `WSADATA`, `CRITICAL_SECTION`, a
COM vtable) adapted by the runtime; `stl` and `stlio` the C++ runtime (`msvcp140`) under x86
mangled names the x64 DLL does not export; `cpp`, `com` and `engine` the same C++ runtime and
exceptions, plus instructions the lift does not cover yet (`com`).
